scope: Dependency map of every link a theory of everything would need, with the current evidence for each. Not a proof score or completion percentage.

status_vocabulary.stipulated: Supplied model input or assumption; not derived.
status_vocabulary.exact_theorem: Proved within its stated model and hypotheses.
status_vocabulary.controlled_limit: Proved in a stated limit or regime only.
status_vocabulary.conditional: Follows if named, unproven hypotheses hold.
status_vocabulary.calibrated: A number fixed by matching data, not predicted.
status_vocabulary.phenomenological_fit: Formula or ansatz with fitted or chosen inputs.
status_vocabulary.obstructed: A proved or verified obstruction within a stated class; other classes remain open.
status_vocabulary.open: No result yet; a well-posed problem is named.
status_vocabulary.withdrawn: Claim falsified or withdrawn; kept for the record.

link_vocabulary.premises: Map nodes whose results this node's claim actually uses, each with a reason. A stipulated node has none. For an open node they are the objects the problem is posed on.
link_vocabulary.context: Map nodes that motivated or frame this node without being used by its result, each with a reason.
link_vocabulary.hypotheses: Named unproven assumptions the node's status rests on. 'node' names a map node when the assumption is that node's unproven content. Every conditional node names at least one.
link_vocabulary.depends_on: Union of premises and context, kept for one release for compatibility; read premises and context instead.

premise_audit.rule: For an audited node, every node reachable through premises must have a permitted status unless the audited node names it in hypotheses. Axioms are the stipulated nodes reachable through premises (an analogue of Lean's #print axioms); they list map nodes only.

verification_vocabulary.none: No check of the stated content is recorded. Used for stipulated inputs, open problems and withdrawn claims.
verification_vocabulary.argument: A written derivation or computation exists in the repository; no independent review section is recorded for it.
verification_vocabulary.ai_review: AI review of scoped mathematics, not certification: an independent adversarial review by a separate AI agent is recorded under a heading in a derivation note (review.anchor). Such reviews can miss errors; the repository's own review records show repairs after review.
verification_vocabulary.exact_computation: As ai_review, and named pytest tests (exact_checks) check the claim's computational core in exact integer, rational, finite-field or symbolic arithmetic against an independent oracle. scope states what those tests do not cover; the reduction from the physical statement to that core remains argument plus review.
verification_vocabulary.formal_statement: The statement is fixed in a proof assistant; its proof is not machine-checked. Not used: BPR has no Lean formalization.
verification_vocabulary.formal_proof: A machine-checked proof of the exact formal statement, with a comparator configuration (verification.formal). Not used: BPR has no Lean formalization. It would cover only the formal statement, never the physics reduction.

review_kinds.ai_adversarial: An independent review by a separate AI agent instructed to look for errors.
review_kinds.human: A review by a named human expert. None is recorded.

verification_note: Verification records how far a node's content has been checked; status records what kind of claim it is. No percentage of nodes at any level is computed: it would depend on the denominator and would read as a proof score.

nodes.limitation: Round sphere assumed; the SU(2) family gauge bosons need a high-scale breaking that is not supplied.

nodes.claim: Yukawa couplings of the three flux families in BPR-6D.

premises.reason: The selection rule acts on these flux families.

nodes.limitation: The minimal content has no field in 16x16 = 10+120+126, so no Yukawa at all. For extensions, an all-orders selection rule (perturbative in U(1)_F) leaves only an F-charge -2 (-6 in parent-charge-3 units) internal one-form 10 or 126 in the J=2 channel; scalars and the 120 never couple. SO(12) gauge-Higgs gives paired, even families and a vacuum instability. 10-only Higgs gives M_d = M_e^T (excluded); complex J=2 vevs reach every spectrum, so no mass ratio is predicted. Round 8: a brane Higgs has J_z charge c = s_h + 3, so a brane scalar never couples and a normal-bundle vector gives rank 1; with J_z exact one brane never gives three distinct masses; clustered vector branes or J_z broken at a brane (Heckman-Vafa) give the Froggatt-Nielsen form (1, eps^2, eps^4) with eps free, so no hierarchy is predicted; every route needs the ~1e-30 weak-scale tuning.

nodes.claim: BPR-6D admits a string-theory (supersymmetric F-theory) embedding.

premises.reason: The question is posed for the quantized model; the Morrison-Taylor tension concerns its charge-q/3 states.

nodes.limitation: The Morrison-Taylor massless-charge statement is supersymmetric, and BPR-6D meets its premise (-a.b~ = 24) only in a chirality convention (no gravitino). A massless vector-like charge-1 pair removes the tension without changing anomalies or families, but its masslessness is unprotected. Supersymmetric analogues: on T=0 the charge normalization is never forced (Lemma 3, any gauge group) and a gcd-1 spectrum still has 3 net families; on T=1 (the counterpart of one non-chiral 2-form) anomaly cancellation can force charges into 3Z. The fork is anomaly-forced 3 | n_gen vs F-theory embeddability. No vacuum or F-theory construction is given.

nodes.claim: The compactification breaks Spin(10) to the Standard Model.

premises.reason: The orbifold family counts use the families' SU(2) triplet structure.
The Green-Schwarz BF vector that makes the flux direction massive comes from the quantized coupling.

nodes.limitation: Every quantized Spin(10) flux on the round S^2 is unstable (a root with |alpha.h| >= 2 gives a tachyonic W; pi_1(Spin(10)) = 0). Even if stabilized, the Green-Schwarz BF vector (18m, 3h) makes the flux direction massive, so no flux keeps SU(3) x SU(2) with a massless hypercharge (standard or flipped); the flux would be chirality-neutral (3 net families). Rotation orbifolds of S^2 keep at most 2 (Z2) or 1 families per multiplet. Conventional Higgs breaking remains possible but is supplied, not derived.

nodes.claim: Brane tensions on the BPR-6D sphere self-tune the 4D cosmological constant.

premises.reason: The football solutions deform this vacuum with brane tensions.

nodes.limitation: Classical football solutions with the flux quantum conserved: H = 0 forces u = M^4/(2 Lambda) and B^2 = 2 Lambda on either root, pinning the deficit, so flat tensions are discrete (one per flux quantum) and dH^2/dT = sqrt(2) e sqrt(Lambda)/(3 pi m M^4) > 0 at the flat point; brane vacuum energy is not absorbed (Navarro 2003; Garriga-Porrati). Unwarped, equal-tension ansatz; breathing-mode stability only. Supersymmetric SLED routes are cited and contested; in an F-theory embedding 3 | n_gen would be allowed but not forced.

nodes.claim: With a supplied Higgs sector, U(1)_F acts as a Peccei-Quinn symmetry; given a supplied F-charged Standard-Model singlet, BPR-6D has an invisible QCD axion with f <~ f_b/3 (~1e14 to 1e17 GeV); n_gen in 3Z.

premises.reason: The axion couplings come from the quantized Green-Schwarz term.
The decay-constant band uses the compactification scales of this vacuum.

hypotheses.name: supplied_higgs_sector
hypotheses.statement: A Higgs sector is supplied; with it U(1)_F acts as a Peccei-Quinn symmetry.

hypotheses.name: supplied_f_charged_singlet
hypotheses.statement: An F-charged Standard-Model singlet S with a DFSZ-type link is supplied. With only the Higgs doublets the axion is an excluded PQWW axion.

nodes.limitation: theta-bar = theta_0 + 3b + 3 arg(H_u H_d) + ... is gauge invariant and the dual axion a does not enter. With only the Higgs doublets the axion is an excluded PQWW axion (f ~ 41 GeV); an instanton-generated H_u H_d term pins theta-bar; a viable axion needs a supplied singlet S (f ~ min(f_b/3, f_S/c_S)). The band depends on the unfixed 2-form coupling; axion quality is unresolved; superradiance disfavours f >~ 3e17 GeV. The axion is generic to Green-Schwarz models. n_gen in 3Z is a postdiction for class C. Masses, mixings, Higgs mass, GUT scale and the cosmological constant are not predicted. No test against data is made.

nodes.claim: A definite minimal BPR-6D model (Phase 1): bulk 45_H plus a single bulk complex 10_H and 126bar_H of F-charge -6, coupled at four branes through eth-bar operators, and a brane singlet S; it breaks Spin(10) exactly to the SM, realizes generic Yukawa pairs modulo U(3), and unifies at one loop with proton decay far above the Super-K bound.

premises.reason: Its coupling rules (only F-charge -6 Higgs fields in J = 2 couple; point couplings need c = 2) fix the Higgs content and the brane operators.
Kill check 6 (a viable axion) uses the axion analysis, and the singlet S is added because of it.
The model lives on this compactification.
The families and their SU(2) structure are those of the flux sphere.

context.reason: Geometric breaking is obstructed, which is why a 45_H breaking Higgs is supplied.

hypotheses.name: cited_vacuum_and_fits
hypotheses.statement: The 45 + 126 breaking vacuum and the fermion fits the model relies on are cited, not derived.

hypotheses.name: one_loop_survival
hypotheses.statement: Gauge running is one loop under the survival hypothesis (M_I ~ 1e9 GeV).

hypotheses.name: brane_moduli_stabilized
hypotheses.statement: The five brane-position moduli, which couple to fermions, are stabilized. This is not shown and is potentially fatal (kill check 11).

nodes.limitation: The brane-copy version fails (rank-1 tree Yukawas; three Delta_R leave no consistent intermediate scale). The adopted bulk-Higgs version passes the computed checks but: the Higgs content is chosen; the 45+126 vacuum and the fermion fits are cited; running is one-loop under the survival hypothesis (M_I ~ 1e9 GeV, seesaw tension possibly an artifact); the compactification window 1/r ~ (2-8)e16 GeV is not robust; five brane-position moduli couple to fermions and are unstabilized (potentially fatal); no fermion mass is predicted (21 parameters for 15 effective); Higgs mass, M_I hierarchy and Lambda are tuned.

nodes.claim: Phase 1d: a bulk SO(10)-singlet scalar chi of U(1)_F charge -4 has a spin-2 lowest level whose profiles have exactly four zeros; in the type-II regime its quartic is minimized by the tetrahedral state (|2,2> + sqrt2 |2,-1>)/sqrt3 (energy 25/(84 pi), five positive Hessian modes), and brane terms kappa |chi(z_a)|^2 pin the four branes at its zeros, a regular tetrahedron.

premises.reason: The four branes and their couplings are this model's.
chi lives on this flux sphere; its charge fixes the spin of its lowest level.

hypotheses.name: chi_supplied
hypotheses.statement: The charge -4 bulk scalar chi and its brane terms are added, not derived.

hypotheses.name: type_ii_regime
hypotheses.statement: chi's quartic is in the type-II regime, where the tetrahedral state is its minimum.

hypotheses.name: pinning_survives
hypotheses.statement: The uncomputed one-loop brane forces do not undo the metastable pinning, and vr lies in the narrow window 1.75 <~ vr <~ 2.45.

nodes.limitation: chi is added, not derived. The pinning is metastable at best: stacking two branes on one zero costs no pinning energy, the barrier between vortices is 5/(16 pi) kappa (vr)^2/r^4, and the one-loop brane forces are not computed; the window 1.75 <~ vr <~ 2.45 is narrow and not robust. Identical branes give zero Yukawas, so A4 must be broken at O(1) by the brane couplings. Fixed positions restrict the reachable Yukawa pairs to a proper subset (Phase 2 finds this subset fails the charged-fermion data).

nodes.claim: Phase 2: with free brane positions the minimal non-SUSY 10 + 126bar sector with a type-I seesaw fits the charged-fermion and neutrino data (one-loop SM running, assumed GUT-scale errors): best chi^2 = 2.9 for 17 observables and 18 physical parameters (-1 dof), normal ordering only (inverted chi^2 ~ 4e4). With the branes pinned at the Phase 1d tetrahedron, H and F must be pure J = 2 and annihilated by the pinning condensate in some family basis; the best pinned fits found have chi^2 ~ 120 (73 for the charged sector alone), with m_s about 3.6-3.9 times too large.

premises.reason: Fits this model's 10 + 126bar sector.
The pinned case uses this tetrahedron.

verification.scope: A reviewed fit, not a validation; see the limitation.

nodes.limitation: No empirical validation: the free-position fit has -1 degrees of freedom, so it shows consistency, not a test; its stable consequences (normal ordering, sum m_nu ~ 0.06-0.07 eV, m_betabeta ~ 0.4 meV) follow from the fit, while sin delta_CP and M_R are not stable. It needs v_R >~ 4e11 GeV, 400-1000 times the one-loop M_I. The pinned failure is leading order (Phase 2b: normalization corrections do not repair it at natural size, but a one-derivative brane vertex of the same order can) and rests on searches, not a proof of the global minimum. Running is one loop with an 8% theory error; errors and inputs are assumed or recalled.

nodes.claim: Phase 2b: next-to-leading corrections to the pinned flavour structure. Normalization corrections (brane kinetic terms, tension distortion) act only through the family kinetic matrix, Y -> A Y A^T with A = Kbar^{-1/2}; equal or A4-symmetric ones are trivial (tight frame, Schur), and an O(1) kinetic matrix erases pinning (projective equivalence; exact positive control). At natural size they leave chi^2 >~ 40 (charged) and >~ 90 (with neutrinos). The one-derivative brane vertex 16 (eth 16) (ethbar^2 Phi), allowed by the same J_z rule and of the same order, adds pure-J=2 pieces outside the pinned subspace and fits: charged sector at |delta| <= 0.1, all data at |delta| <= 0.3 (chi^2 = 4.5), at or just above the top of its natural range 0.07-0.25. Pinning is not excluded at next-to-leading order, but flavour is not predicted.

premises.reason: Uses its fit machinery, inputs and pinned best point.
The corrections act on this pinned tetrahedral structure.

verification.scope: Search-based upper bounds; the review checked the stored values against the code.

nodes.limitation: Search-based upper bounds, not a proof: bounded local optimizations (homotopy, restarts, polish, re-seeding); some with-neutrino rows are rugged. Natural sizes are unit-coefficient estimates (strong coupling could raise them by up to 8 pi); tension effects are estimated, not computed. Non-universal SO(10)-breaking brane terms and two-derivative vertices are not included. The vertex rescue adds 16 real parameters and relaxes the condensate condition, so pinning constrains flavour no more than free positions. Inputs and errors as in Phase 2. Found by the independent review, which reversed the first version's verdict.
